HON'BLE
MR. JUSTICE KULDEEP MATHUR

Order 20/11/2024 This criminal revision petition under Section 379 read with Section 401 of the Cr.P.C. has been preferred by the petitioner against the judgment dated 11.07.2005 passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Phalodi, District Jodhpur in Cr. Appeal No.02/2005 whereby the judgment dated 10.02.2005 passed by the learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Phalodi in Cr. Original Case No.177/1998 was modified to the extent of sentences awarded to the present petitioner.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge, Phalodi, District Jodhpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The learned Appelant court vide its order dated 11.07.2005 thus convicted and sentenced the petitioner for the offences as mentioned below:
Conviction for offence under Sentence(s) Section:
7/16 of Prevention of Food Six months' simple Adulteration Act imprisonment and a fine of Rs.1000/-, and in default of payment of fine to further undergo one months'
simple [2024:RJ-JD:47681] (2 of 4) [CRLR-596/2005] imprisonment.
The record of the case file shows that the complainant (food inspector) filed a complaint before the learned ACJM, Phalodi alleging inter alia that the petitioner who is a milk vendor and usually sells milk outside the railway station, Phalodi, on 16.12.1997, was found selling milk without lisence.

Thereafter, the complainant took a Sukh Ram vs State (2024:Rj-Jd:47681) on 20 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182475706/
1 sample of 750ml of milk from the petitioner and sent it to the Public Analyst for analysis.
Upon the report of Public Analyst, the milk was found to be adulterated.

On the basis of the said complaint, the learned ACJM framed charges against the petitioner for offence punishable under Section 7/16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and the petitioner denied the same and demanded trial.
After hearing both the parties, the learned trial Court convicted and sentenced the petitioner for the aforesaid offence.

Learned counsel for the revisionist-petitioner submitted that the sentences so awarded to the revisionist-petitioner were suspended by this Court, vide order dated 27.07.2005 in S.B.Cr. Misc.
Bail (Suspension of Sentences) Application No.129/2005.

entities.text:
S.B.Cr. Misc.
Bail (Suspension of Sentences) Application No.129/2005
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner has undergone detention for some period and the case is pending against him since 1998.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner is facing agony of a long protracted trial and therefore, without making any interference on merits/conviction, the sentences awarded to the present revisionist-petitioner may be substituted with the period of sentences already undergone by him.
[CRLR-596/2005] Learned Public Prosecutor opposes the submissions made on behalf of the petitioner.
However, he was not in a position to dispute that the present revision petition is pending since 2005.
Heard.
A perusal of the impugned judgments makes is manifest that the alleged incident happened in the year 1997 and the present revision petition is pending adjudication since 2005.

Hon'ble the Supreme Court of India in the case of Alister Anthony PareiraVs. State of Maharashtra (2012)2 SCC 648 andHaripada Das Vs. State of W.B. (1998)9 SCC 678, pleased to observe as under:
Alister Anthony Pareira (supra) "There is no straitjacket formula for sentencing an accused on proof of crime.

entities.text: Alister Anthony PareiraVs. State of Maharashtra (2012)2 SCC 648
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: andHaripada Das Vs. State of W.B. (1998)9 SCC 678
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The courts have evolved certain principles: twin objective of the sentencing policy is deterrence and correction.

What sentence would meet the ends of justice depends on the facts and circumstances of each case and the court must keep in mind the gravity of the crime, motive for the crime, nature of the offence and all other attendant circumstances."

Haripada Das (supra) "... considering the fact that the respondent had already undergone detention for some period and the case is pending for a pretty long time for which he had suffered both financial hardship and mental agony and also considering the fact that he had been released on bail as far back as on 17-1-1986, we feel that the ends of justice will be met in the facts of the case if the sentence is reduced to the period already undergone..."

Sukh Ram vs State (2024:Rj-Jd:47681) on 20 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182475706/
2

In the light of aforesaid discussion, precedent law and keeping in view the limited prayer made on behalf of the [2024:RJ-JD:47681] (4 of 4) [CRLR-596/2005]
revisionist-petitioner, the present revision petition is partly allowed.

Accordingly, while maintaining the conviction of the petitioner for the offenceunder Section 7/16 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, the sentences awarded to the petitioner are hereby reduced to the period already undergone by him.
The petitioner isalready enlarged on bail.
He need not surrender.
His bail bonds stand discharged accordingly.
All pending applications stand disposed of.
Record of the case be sent back to the learned Courts below forthwith.

(KULDEEP MATHUR),J 13-himanshu/-
